svg.aria-label: Fig. M8 Translation, the two TLBs and the walk
svg.text: Fig. M8 Translation, the two TLBs and the walk
16 KiB pages, 48 bit virtual addresses. The set index bits are measured; the walk levels follow from the ARM 16 KiB granule.
Virtual address as the TLBs and the walker slice it
page walk for a 16 KiB granule and 48 bit VA (derived from the ISA): three full levels plus a one bit level 0 index at bit 47
L1 table index 46:36
L2 table index 35:25
L3 index 24:14
page offset 13:0
tag
L2 TLB set 21:14
offset
L1 dTLB set = VA 18:14 (5 bits, 32 sets x 5 ways = 160, corroborated). L2 TLB set = VA 21:14 (8 bits, 256 sets x 12 ways = 3072, single source).
L1 dTLB
160 entries, confirmed
entry
VA tag 46:19 | ASID | PA frame | perm index | size
one lookup per cycle (derived), shared with queued requests
to the same page by piggybacking (inferred)
replacement looks random: latency past capacity climbs
linearly from 3 to 9 cycles instead of stepping (inferred)
also the backing store for the two L1 iTLBs (user, kernel):
translations evicted from an iTLB land here (inferred)
miss penalty 6 cycles to the L2 TLB (single source)
Proposed: with 3 loads a cycle and one lookup, the
piggyback must cover most of the traffic; a probe
with 3 loads a cycle to 3 different pages should
fall to 1 per cycle if the TLB really has one port.
L2 TLB
3072 entries, confirmed
12 ways x 256 sets
miss penalty 25 cycles including the walk start (corroborated)
Cluster shared L2 TLB and walkers beside the L2 (patent):
if so the 25 cycles include a trip over the L1 to L2 path,
and a second core's misses contend for it.
Test (mine): two cores each thrashing their L1 dTLB but
hitting the L2 TLB. Per core cost rises if the L2 TLB is
shared and single ported, stays flat if private.
Only 16 KiB pages observed on the M1 (single source).
Page walk
inferred
MMU walk cache
caches the upper two levels (L1, L2 tables)
leaf entries read from the L2 cache
walk = 1 walk cache hit + 1 L2 access, about 17 + a few cycles
so a 25 cycle L2 TLB miss leaves 8 for TLB and walker logic
Permissions by index (patent): a page holds an index into a
4 entry permission table, so one core can switch a page's
permissions with no TLB shootdown.
Invalidation (patent): range invalidate picks scanning or
per page lookup; ASID and VMID compared four at a time.
Speculative faults: a load through a pointer that failed its
AUT check is not performed and leaves no TLB trace (measured).
iTLB: 192 entries (measured) against a 4 way 32 set shape
that gives 128; shape and size do not fit, open.
Latency ladder for a load by where its translation and data are found
